verdict.rationale: The MCP authentication docs name at least one OAuth-style scope (`context:protected:read`) gating protected context, so access is scope-partitioned to some degree. The hosted MCP uses a standard OAuth protected-resource pattern with a separate authorization server, and the CLI uses a device-code login an agent can drive up to human approval. However, nothing shows a user deliberately issuing a dedicated, narrowly scoped credential (API key or token) for an agent; agents appear to act under the signed-in user's account and organization. missing for 10: documented way to mint agent-specific API keys/tokens, user-selectable scope or permission sets, a full scope catalog, credential revocation/rotation and expiry controls, independent or hands-on corroboration of scoped issuance. [2026-10-08 adversarial bias audit (owner-product bring-up lane): reverted partial 3 -> none 0 — the story is issuing scoped/least-privilege credentials for an agent; the rationale concedes nothing shows a user issuing a dedicated scoped credential, and one scope name in the MCP auth docs is not an issuance capability. Every peer with no issuance surface sits at none/na. Ultrametric-affiliation governance, README §9.]
